Merarites
me-RAR-ites
n. pl.
The descendants of Merari, Levi’s third son, whose name is connected with the Hebrew for bitterness. Their charge was the frame of the tabernacle — boards, bars, pillars, sockets, pins, and cords — the heaviest burden and the least visible when the house was standing.

Biblical Definition

The Merarites carried the skeleton of the house of God. Under the custody and charge of the sons of Merari shall be the boards of the tabernacle, and the bars thereof, and the pillars thereof, and the sockets thereof, and all the vessels thereof, and all that serveth thereto (Numbers 3:36), and the charge is repeated at Numbers 4:31 with the pins and cords added. Four wagons and eight oxen were assigned them, twice what Gershon received, because the load was silver sockets and acacia boards overlaid with gold. Nothing they carried was ever seen once the tabernacle was pitched; the curtains covered the boards, and the boards held everything else up. The clan is one of the three named in the census of Levi: of Gershon, the family of the Gershonites: of Kohath, the family of the Kohathites: of Merari, the family of the Merarites (Numbers 26:57). They kept their office for a thousand years. When David set the singers over the service of song in the house of the LORD, Ethan the son of Kishi of the sons of Merari stood on the left hand with Asaph on the right and Heman in the midst. And when Hezekiah opened the temple doors, Kish the son of Abdi and Azariah the son of Jehalelel came up of the sons of Merari with the rest.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 has no MERARITE entry. The Hebrew Merari is generally traced to marar, to be bitter — the same root as Marah, Mara, and the bitter herbs of the passover.

expand to see more

MERARITE, n. — A descendant of Merari, the third son of Levi; one of the Levitical clan charged with the boards, bars, pillars, and sockets of the tabernacle.

Numbers 3:33 names their two families: the Mahlites and the Mushites.

They pitched on the north side of the tabernacle, under Zuriel the son of Abihail (Numbers 3:35).

Four wagons and eight oxen were given to their service (Numbers 7:8), the load being the heaviest of the three clans.

Webster 1828 does not treat the word; Numbers, Joshua 21, and 1 Chronicles 6 and 26 supply the biblical usage.

Key Scripture

Numbers 3:36 — "And under the custody and charge of the sons of Merari shall be the boards of the tabernacle, and the bars thereof, and the pillars thereof, and the sockets thereof, and all the vessels thereof, and all that serveth thereto,"

Numbers 4:31 — "And this is the charge of their burden, according to all their service in the tabernacle of the congregation; the boards of the tabernacle, and the bars thereof, and the pillars thereof, and sockets thereof,"

Numbers 26:57 — "And these are they that were numbered of the Levites after their families: of Gershon, the family of the Gershonites: of Kohath, the family of the Kohathites: of Merari, the family of the Merarites."

Numbers 10:21 — "And the Kohathites set forward, bearing the sanctuary: and the other did set up the tabernacle against they came."

2 Chronicles 29:12 — "Then the Levites arose, Mahath the son of Amasai, and Joel the son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites: and of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi, and Azariah the son of Jehalelel: and of the Gershonites; Joah the son of Zimmah, and Eden the son of Joah:"

Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the heaviest and least visible labour in the house of God is a named, numbered, divinely assigned office — not the residue left over when the honoured work is distributed.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Numbers 10:21 contains a small, easily missed sentence: the Kohathites came forward bearing the sanctuary, and the other did set up the tabernacle against they came. The margin identifies the other as the Gershonites and Merarites. That is, the men carrying the boards went ahead, raised the frame, and had the house standing before the ark arrived. Nobody watching the procession was looking at them. Their work was finished before the holy things appeared and invisible the moment the curtains went on. Scripture nevertheless records their families, their prince, their wagons, their oxen, and their exact inventory down to the pins and the cords.

This is the pattern for how a church should think about its unseen labour, and Reformed churches with a high view of preaching are as capable as any of getting it wrong. The Merarites did not carry lesser things; they carried the things everything else rested on. Their descendants were still at their post when Hezekiah cleansed the temple and when David appointed the singers, and Ethan the Merarite stood beside Asaph in the service of song. A family that keeps an unglamorous charge for a thousand years has done something the church should know how to name. Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Merari (H4847), bitter, from marar (H4843) to be bitter; the gentilic is Merari used adjectivally, Merarite (H4848).

expand to see more

Hebrew Merari (H4847) — Merari; third son of Levi (Genesis 46:11; Exodus 6:16).

Hebrew marar (H4843) — to be bitter; the root also behind Marah (Exodus 15:23) and Naomi’s call me Mara.

Hebrew Merari (H4848) — Merarite; the clan name of Numbers 26:57 and 1 Chronicles 26:19.

Hebrew qeresh (H7175) — a board of the tabernacle; the chief item of their burden (Numbers 3:36).

Hebrew eden (H134) — a socket or base, of silver, into which the boards were set; the foundation of the whole structure.

Usage

"The boards of the tabernacle, and the bars thereof (Numbers 3:36) — the frame everything else rested on."

"The other did set up the tabernacle against they came (Numbers 10:21) — the house standing before the ark arrived."

"Of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi (2 Chronicles 29:12) — the clan still at its post under Hezekiah."
